title: Romans Bible Quiz - Chapter 15
description: Ten questions on Romans 15: bearing the weaknesses of the weak, the Gentiles glorifying God, and the writer's travel and offering plans.

questions.text: Who ought to bear the weaknesses of the weak?
questions.explanation: Romans 15:1 says that we who are strong ought to bear the weaknesses of the weak, and not to please ourselves.

answers.text: The elders only
Those who are weak themselves
The rulers of the city
Those who are strong

questions.text: What is written about Christ, who did not please himself?
questions.explanation: Romans 15:3 says that even Christ did not please himself, but as it is written, “The reproaches of those who reproached you fell on me.”

answers.text: “He was led as a lamb to the slaughter.”
“Not my will, but yours be done.”
“The reproaches of those who reproached you fell on me.”
“He bore our griefs and carried our sorrows.”

questions.text: Why were the things written before written, according to the text?
questions.explanation: Romans 15:4 says whatever things were written before were written for our learning, so that through perseverance and encouragement of the Scriptures we might have hope.

answers.text: To condemn the disobedient
For our learning, that we might have hope
To be read only by the priests
To settle disputes among the nations

questions.text: What was Christ made a servant of the circumcision to confirm?
questions.explanation: Romans 15:8 says Christ has been made a servant of the circumcision for the truth of God, that he might confirm the promises given to the fathers.

answers.text: The promises given to the fathers
The ordinances of the temple
The boundaries of the land
The counsel of the prophets

questions.text: Isaiah says there will be the root of whom, who arises to rule over the Gentiles?
questions.explanation: Romans 15:12 quotes Isaiah saying there will be the root of Jesse, who arises to rule over the Gentiles, and in him the Gentiles will hope.

answers.text: David
Abraham
Judah
Jesse

questions.text: How far does the writer say he had fully preached the Good News of Christ?
questions.explanation: Romans 15:19 says that in the power of signs and wonders and of God's Spirit, from Jerusalem and around as far as to Illyricum, he had fully preached the Good News of Christ.

answers.text: From Antioch as far as Rome
From Corinth as far as Spain
From Jerusalem as far as Illyricum
From Judea as far as Egypt

questions.text: What was his aim in preaching the Good News?
questions.explanation: Romans 15:20 says he made it his aim to preach the Good News not where Christ was already named, so that he would not build on another's foundation.

answers.text: To preach only in large cities
To preach where Christ was not already named
To preach where he had friends
To preach only to his own relatives

questions.text: To which country did he say he would travel?
questions.explanation: Romans 15:24 says that whenever he travels to Spain he will come to them, hoping to see them on his journey.

answers.text: Spain
Egypt
Cyprus
Syria

questions.text: For whom had Macedonia and Achaia made a contribution?
questions.explanation: Romans 15:26 says it was the good pleasure of Macedonia and Achaia to make a certain contribution for the poor among the saints who are at Jerusalem.

answers.text: The widows of the assembly at Corinth
The prisoners who were held at Rome
The teachers of the assemblies of the Gentiles
The poor among the saints at Jerusalem

questions.text: What does the writer beg his brothers to do for him?
questions.explanation: Romans 15:30 begs them, by our Lord Jesus Christ and by the love of the Spirit, to strive together with him in their prayers to God for him.

answers.text: Send him money for the journey to Spain
Write letters on his behalf to the saints
Strive together with him in their prayers to God
Go before him to Spain and prepare the way
